localities.name: Koramangala
localities.description: Premier startup hub in south Bangalore. Home to restaurants, tech offices, and vibrant nightlife. High demand drives premium rents. 6–10 months deposit typical.

localities.name: Indiranagar
localities.description: Upscale locality with Metro connectivity, restaurants, and nightlife. Very high demand from IT professionals. Deposits at 8–10 months are common.

localities.name: HSR Layout
localities.description: Planned layout with wide roads, parks, and excellent social infrastructure. Popular with startup founders and IT workers. Close to Koramangala and Bellandur.

localities.name: Whitefield
localities.description: Major IT hub with ITPL and large tech campuses. Metro extended to Whitefield in 2023. Longer commute to central Bangalore but good local amenities.

localities.name: Marathahalli
localities.description: High-density residential area near Outer Ring Road. Popular with Whitefield/Bellandur IT professionals. Good eateries and shopping.

localities.name: Bellandur
localities.description: Rapidly developing area near Outer Ring Road and Sarjapur Road. Many gated communities. The lake area has had water quality issues — check proximity when renting.

localities.name: Electronic City
localities.description: Major IT hub (Infosys, Wipro campuses). Metro connectivity via elevated corridor. More affordable than central areas. 2–5 months deposit typical.

localities.name: JP Nagar
localities.description: Large, well-planned residential area in south Bangalore. Good Metro connectivity, BDA parks, and markets. Family-friendly with quieter roads.

localities.name: Jayanagar
localities.description: One of Bangalore's oldest planned localities. Well-connected via Metro. Popular with Kannadiga families. High demand drives 6–10 month deposits.

localities.name: BTM Layout
localities.description: Busy residential area between Jayanagar and Koramangala. Good restaurants and local transport. Popular with young professionals and IT workers.

localities.name: Hebbal
localities.description: North Bangalore hub with proximity to airport. Good Metro access. Embassy and IT office zones nearby. Flyover area prone to traffic during peak hours.

localities.name: Yelahanka
localities.description: Large township in north Bangalore. More affordable, quieter. Good for families. IAF station area. Some parts still developing. Close to airport.

localities.name: Banashankari
localities.description: Established residential locality with Metro access. Known for temples and peaceful environment. Good BMTC connectivity.

localities.name: Malleshwaram
localities.description: Heritage locality in northwest Bangalore. Cultural hub with Rajajinagar market, temples, old Bangalore charm. High demand from established families.

localities.name: Sarjapur Road
localities.description: Fast-developing corridor with many IT parks and gated communities. Good for families. Traffic can be heavy during peak hours.

rights.title: Security Deposit: Your Right to Get It Back
rights.content:
# Security Deposit: Your Right to Get It Back

**⚠️ Not legal advice. Consult a qualified advocate for your specific situation.**

## What is a Security Deposit?

A security deposit (also called "advance" in Bangalore) is money you pay your landlord before moving in, to be refunded when you move out. In Bangalore, this is typically 2–10 months' rent depending on the locality.

## Timeline for Return

The Karnataka Rent Act 1999 does not specify an exact number of days for deposit return. However, courts have consistently held that deposit should be returned within 1–2 months of vacating. Any deductions must be communicated in writing with itemized bills.

## What Can Be Deducted?

✅ Landlord CAN deduct for actual physical damage, unpaid rent, unpaid utility bills.
❌ Landlord CANNOT deduct for normal wear and tear, routine maintenance, repainting (unless walls are genuinely damaged).

## Steps to Recover Your Deposit

1. Send a formal demand letter citing the move-out date
2. Keep records: move-in/out photos, rent receipts, utility bills  
3. File a complaint with the Rent Control Authority / Rent Court if landlord refuses
4. For amounts above ₹2 lakh, engage an advocate
rights.excerpt: Your landlord must return your security deposit after you vacate. Learn the timelines, deductions they can and cannot make, and what to do if they refuse.

rights.title: Rent Increase Rules in Karnataka
rights.content:
# Rent Increase Rules in Karnataka

**⚠️ Not legal advice. Consult a qualified advocate for your specific situation.**

Your landlord cannot increase rent during the fixed term of your lease. At renewal, typical annual increase in Bangalore is 5–10%. Above 20% per year is unusual and potentially exploitative.

## Karnataka Rent Act 1999 Applicability

The Act applies to residential premises where monthly rent does not exceed ₹3,500. Most Bangalore rentals exceed this threshold.
rights.excerpt: Your landlord cannot increase rent unilaterally during a lease term. Know the rules, typical annual increase norms, and your rights to dispute an unfair hike.

rights.title: Eviction Notice Periods and Your Protection
rights.content:
# Eviction Notice Periods and Your Protection

**⚠️ Not legal advice. 🔖 Lawyer verification recommended.**

Minimum notice periods: Month-to-month tenancy (1 month), Fixed-term lease (per agreement), Non-payment (15 days demand).

Illegal eviction tactics include cutting electricity/water, changing locks, removing belongings. Call police if this happens.
rights.excerpt: Your landlord must give you proper notice before asking you to vacate. Know the minimum notice periods, grounds for eviction, and what constitutes illegal eviction.

rights.title: Landlord Entry and Your Right to Privacy
rights.content:
# Landlord Entry and Your Right to Privacy

**⚠️ Not legal advice.**

Your landlord must give at least 24 hours advance notice before entry. Entry is only for agreed purposes (repairs, inspection). The exception is genuine emergencies (gas leak, fire, flooding).

Insist on lease clause: "Landlord shall provide at least 24 hours prior written notice before entering except in genuine emergencies."
rights.excerpt: Your rented home is your private space. Your landlord cannot enter without prior notice. Learn your privacy rights and how to assert them.

rights.title: Rent Agreements: 11-Month vs Registered Leases
rights.content:
# Rent Agreements: 11-Month vs Registered Leases

**⚠️ Not legal advice.**

Leases for 12+ months must be registered under Registration Act 1908. 11-month leases avoid this requirement. Registered leases offer stronger legal protection. For long tenancies, insist on registration.

Kaveri Online Services for registration: https://kaverionline.karnataka.gov.in
rights.excerpt: Why do most leases in Bangalore say "11 months"? What is the difference between registered and unregistered agreements? Which gives you better protection?

rights.title: Police Verification for Tenants
rights.content:
# Police Verification for Tenants

**⚠️ Not legal advice.**

Tenants must complete police verification within 30 days of moving in. Online at: https://ksp.karnataka.gov.in

Documents required: Aadhaar, PAN card, rent agreement copy, landlord's ID and property documents, passport-size photographs.
rights.excerpt: Police verification is a legal requirement for tenants in Karnataka. Learn the process, your obligations, and what happens if it is not done.

rights.title: Maintenance and Society Charges: What You Must Pay
rights.content:
# Maintenance and Society Charges

**⚠️ Not legal advice.**

Landlords may pass society maintenance to tenants if disclosed in the agreement. Maintenance charges above 15% of monthly rent without clear breakdown are a red flag. Structural repairs are always the landlord's responsibility.
rights.excerpt: Who pays for maintenance — tenant or landlord? What are society charges, and when are they excessive? Know your rights and obligations.

rights.title: Electricity and Water Billing: Tenant Rights
rights.content:
# Electricity and Water Billing: Tenant Rights

**⚠️ Not legal advice.**

Landlord CANNOT charge commercial (LT-5) BESCOM tariff on a domestic connection. You have the right to see the original BESCOM bill with connection category. BESCOM toll-free: 1912. BWSSB toll-free: 1916.
rights.excerpt: Your landlord cannot charge commercial electricity tariffs on a residential connection. Know how BESCOM and BWSSB billing works.

rights.title: Rent Court and Rent Control Authority: How to File
rights.content:
# Rent Court and Rent Control Authority

**⚠️ Not legal advice. 🔖 Lawyer verification recommended.**

Send a legal notice first (registered post with acknowledgment due). Then file at the City Civil Court. Lok Adalat is faster for amounts below ₹1 lakh.

Online filing: https://efiling.ecourts.gov.in
rights.excerpt: If your landlord refuses to return your deposit, files wrongful eviction, or violates your lease, you can approach the Rent Court.

rights.title: How to Send a Legal Notice to Your Landlord
rights.content:
# How to Send a Legal Notice to Your Landlord

**⚠️ Not legal advice.**

Send by registered post with acknowledgment due (RPAD). Include: your name and address, landlord's name and address, property address, nature of dispute, amounts involved, demand and deadline (15–30 days), consequence if not complied.

Use DoorSpeaks Deposit Letter Generator for a ready-to-use template.
rights.excerpt: A formal legal notice can resolve many landlord disputes without going to court. Learn what to include, how to send it, and what to expect.

rights.title: Move-In / Move-Out Inspection Checklist
rights.content:
# Move-In / Move-Out Inspection Checklist

**⚠️ Not legal advice.**

Document everything: walls, ceiling, flooring, doors, windows, appliances. Photograph all defects before moving in. Have the landlord sign the checklist. At move-out, repeat and compare with move-in photos.

Use DoorSpeaks Checklist App for a digital version.
rights.excerpt: Protect your deposit by documenting the property condition at move-in and move-out. Use this checklist to record every room and fixture.

rights.title: Stamp Duty for Rent Agreements in Karnataka
rights.content:
# Stamp Duty for Rent Agreements in Karnataka

**⚠️ Not legal advice.**

Stamp duty: 0.1% of total rent + deposit for leases up to 1 year. For ₹25,000/month, 11-month lease with ₹2L deposit: approximately ₹475 stamp duty.

e-Stamping via Kaveri Online Services: https://kaverionline.karnataka.gov.in

Unstamped agreements are not admissible in court until stamp duty + 10x penalty is paid.
rights.excerpt: Understand stamp duty on rent agreements in Karnataka. What must be stamped? How much does it cost? Can an unstamped agreement be used in court?
